proposals.hole: A facade path other than `work claim` can move a leaf from open to in-progress without running the criteria gate, while ACL-A1 tests only the claim command.
proposals.proposed_ac: Every facade operation that can transition a leaf into `in_progress` applies the same empty, rendering, and attestation checks as `work claim`; operations that cannot apply those checks cannot perform that transition.

red_test_sketch.expect: The transition is refused with the same missing-attestation error as `work claim`, and the item remains open.
red_test_sketch.given: An open non-trivial feat leaf with non-empty criteria and no current attestation
red_test_sketch.when: The item is moved to `in_progress` through each facade operation capable of changing status, including an operation other than `work claim`

proposals.hole: The noun-based exemption lets PR-shipping work classified as `chore` bypass attack entirely; the document's own workcli continuations demonstrate such chores, despite the stated purpose covering work that ships a PR.
proposals.proposed_ac: A leaf whose configured delivery is a PR requires a current criteria attestation before implementation or PR delivery regardless of whether its noun is `feat`, `bugfix`, or `chore`; a non-PR chore remains exempt.

red_test_sketch.expect: The operation is refused naming the attack step until the chore has a current attestation.
red_test_sketch.given: A chore leaf assigned to a PR-backed delivery track with non-empty criteria and no attestation
red_test_sketch.when: An agent claims it or attempts to record its PR delivery

proposals.hole: An already-started item can amend its criteria, render the amended bytes, and emit a review round before re-attack because ACL-A4 checks freshness of the rendering but not freshness of the attestation.
proposals.proposed_ac: For a tracker-backed PR round, the panel refuses emission unless the item has an attestation matching its current attackable-document digest, even when the supplied criteria file is byte-equal to the current rendering.

red_test_sketch.expect: Round emission is refused as unattested; it succeeds only after a fresh attack closes and the current digest is attested.
red_test_sketch.given: An in-progress feat whose criteria were attested and then amended, with a criteria file freshly rendered after the amendment
red_test_sketch.when: The review panel emits the next round

proposals.hole: A subagent can be dispatched against amended, unattacked criteria because ACL-A8 constrains the brief's text but never requires the rendered criteria to have a current attestation.
proposals.proposed_ac: For PR-backed work, the briefing workflow refuses to produce or dispatch an implementation brief when the current attackable-document digest lacks an attestation, even if every current criterion is copied verbatim into the brief.

red_test_sketch.expect: Brief production or dispatch is refused until the amended criteria are re-attacked and attested.

red_test_sketch.when: The briefing skill is invoked to dispatch implementation work using the amended rendering

proposals.hole: ACL-A6 reruns the new behavioural-outcome lens over records present during registration but does not require the checker to reject future records that omit that lens; a syntactically closed record can therefore pass without the required attack.
proposals.proposed_ac: The checker rejects every attack record that lacks a completed round from the registered behavioural-outcome lens, including records created after the lens was registered, and names the missing lens.

red_test_sketch.expect: The checker exits nonzero and names the missing behavioural-outcome lens.
red_test_sketch.given: A newly created, otherwise closed attack record whose rounds omit the behavioural-outcome lens
red_test_sketch.when: The whole-repository attack-record gate runs

proposals.hole: The standard requires every edge-case-taxonomy row to be resolved or ruled out per criterion, but no acceptance criterion makes an attack find missing resolutions or prevents such a record from closing.
proposals.proposed_ac: For every behavioural criterion, the attack produces a finding for each unresolved taxonomy row among inverse, empty or boundary, dependency failure, repeated or concurrent invocation, and idempotency; the record cannot close until every row is resolved or ruled out with a reason.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attack reports the omitted taxonomy rows by criterion and the record remains open.
red_test_sketch.given: A criterion set containing a well-formed behavioural criterion but no recorded dependency-failure or concurrency resolution
red_test_sketch.when: The criteria attack runs and its record is checked

proposals.hole: A criterion such as “the gate is green” names an allowed observer, is false before the work, is distinguishable afterward, and converts to a failing test, so it passes ACL-A6 despite reproducing the evidence-shaped criteria the document exists to exclude.
proposals.proposed_ac: The behavioural-outcome lens reports a finding when the claimed outcome is only test success, gate success, artifact presence, byte equality, or another evidence state, unless the criterion also names the externally observable behaviour that evidence demonstrates.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attack reports that the criterion states evidence rather than behaviour.

proposals.hole: The four authoring skills can cite the standard exactly as ACL-A7 requires while continuing to emit criteria that violate it; only citation presence, not authoring behaviour, is tested.
proposals.proposed_ac: Criteria produced by each deployed authoring skill on every tool that deploys it pass the behavioural-outcome and taxonomy checks without findings for representative spec, ticket, grilling, and docs-attached-grilling inputs.

red_test_sketch.expect: Each produced criterion set contains a behavioural outcome with an observer, excludes evidence-only criteria, and records every taxonomy resolution; the attack checker reports no related findings.

proposals.hole: Tracker-born full-text lines need not use the bullet grammar or carry stable unique identifiers, so they can be preserved byte-for-byte while spec-lint and the verdict poster silently parse no criterion or a different set.
proposals.proposed_ac: Every non-citation criterion in a tracker-born or mixed field must round-trip through the single criteria grammar as exactly one uniquely identified criterion in field order; rendering refuses an unparseable line or duplicate identifier by name.

proposals.hole: No criterion requires the edge-case taxonomy to be walked for every criterion, so a set can pass while inverse, boundary, dependency-failure, concurrency, and idempotency rows are absent or ruled out without reasons.

proposals.hole: The slice promises that the behavioural-outcome lens is first-ranked, but no criterion would fail if another lens ran before it.

dispositions.rationale: Rejected. The briefing skill is guidance an agent reads on every tool, including tools without the facade; the claim gate (ACL-D4) precedes any dispatch and the panel's emission refusal (ACL-D7, ACL-A4) catches the review, so a brief-time facade check would duplicate two gates in a place that cannot always reach the facade.

Rejected as already true: the checker reads its lens registry live, so once the behavioural-outcome lens is registered no record lacking it closes, whenever the record was written; the deployed attack skill states this rule.

Rejected. Charter D1 places the edge-case taxonomy on the authoring side, and the edge-cases lens of this very attack is the adversarial walk over it; making closure depend on every row being written per criterion would move an authoring discipline into a record-shape rule.

Rejected. An evaluation of each authoring skill's output on representative inputs is a skill eval, not a criterion of this lifecycle; the gate that catches noncompliant output is the attack itself (ACL-A6), which every criterion set faces before a claim, and ACL-A7 pins what the skills say.

Rejected. Charter D1 places the edge-case taxonomy on the authoring side, and the edge-cases lens of this very attack is the adversarial walk over it; making closure depend on every row being written per criterion would move an authoring discipline into a record-shape rule.
Rejected. First-ranked names the lens's priority of judgment in its mandate (agents-config-9k9.397), not the order of dispatch; dispatch order has no observable effect on the record.

Rejected as already true: the checker reads its lens registry live, so once the behavioural-outcome lens is registered no record lacking it closes, whenever the record was written; the deployed attack skill states this rule.

Rejected as already true: the record contract states that a lens that errored or returned unreadable output has no entry and the round is unfinished; the new lens inherits that rule with the record shape.

Rejected. Two runs of an adversarial model over one revision are not required to produce identical findings, and the spec pins determinism on the checker, not the lens; the taxonomy row says a second round reproduces the finding class, which is a property of the malformed set, not a test of the model.

Rejected. The facade does not run the version-control tool, and ACL-D6 states the ceiling: the files are visible in the branch diff and the CI gate reads what is committed; committing before the claim is the skill's documented step (ACL-A13), not a facade check.
Rejected as already true: the facade's contract states that setting the criteria already in force writes nothing, so the attackable document, the attestation and the gate are untouched.

Rejected as following from ACL-D4 and ACL-D5: the record binds to the document's content, so one round over the document as it stands closes whatever intermediate revisions existed; no criterion is needed for a case the digest rule already decides.

Rejected as already true: the record's bind-by-name rule allows one record per document, so a re-attack overwrites it at its canonical path and the prior round is in history; the attack skill's record contract states this.

Rejected, recorded in the out-of-scope list: each gate hashes or compares at its own moment, and an amendment landing after that moment is caught by the next gate; serializing two backend writes is beyond the facade's boundary.

Rejected as already true: the installer drops any asset whose admission record is incomplete, for every asset, and that behaviour is tested in the installer package; ACL-A14 pins the complete case this skill must meet.
